newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovaks recall Prague envoy after Havel remarks.
newsitem.headline: Slovaks recall Prague envoy after Havel remarks.

text.p: Slovakia, offended by comments from Czech President Vaclav Havel about its prime minister, said on Wednesday it had recalled its envoy to Prague for "consultations".

The move, a diplomatic sign of extreme ire, marked a new low in relations between the two central European neighbours. It followed a demand for a public apology from members of the Slovak government on Tuesday.
"Ambassador Ivan Mjartan has been recalled for consultations on the topical state of mutual relations," Dusan Matulaj, head of the foreign ministry's press department, told Reuters.
The two nations formed one country until the peaceful 1993 split of Czechoslovakia, dubbed the "Velvet Divorce".
Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar last week scrapped his first official visit to Prague, scheduled for later this month, because of Czech criticism of Bratislava.
According to Slovak media reports, Havel suggested that Meciar was "paranoid" in a recent interview with the French daily Le Figaro.
Havel and his office have refused to comment on these reports after requests by local media.
The context of the remarks was that Meciar was over-sensitive to Czech criticism of Slovakia.

"We consider the remarks by President Havel concerning Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar to the French daily Le Figaro as a gross violation of the basic tenets of decency in the communication between representatives of two sovereign and equal republics," a cabinet statement said on Tuesday.
The Czechs and Slovaks have yet to settle numerous issues arising from their 1993 split, such as the division of federal gold reserves and cultural artefacts, and cross-ownership of some banks.

The Czech National Bank has said the federation's gold reserves were split two-to-one in Prague's favour, roughly the same ratio as the two populations as a whole, but the Slovaks argue that Prague still holds a large amount of Slovak gold.
The main purpose of Meciar's planned visit was to sign final agreements on the division of property of the former federation.
